title: OSHA Crane Inspection Checklist (29 CFR 1926.1412)
subtitle: For the shift, monthly and annual/comprehensive inspections of cranes and derricks under 29 CFR 1926.1412.
instructions: Mark every item OK, Defect or N/A; sections A and B apply at the shift, monthly and annual inspections, sections C to E at the annual/comprehensive inspection. For monthly and annual/comprehensive inspections, record the items checked, the results, the inspector's name and signature and the date (1926.1412(e)(3)(i), 1926.1412(f)(7)).

If a shift or monthly item fails, the competent person decides immediately whether it is a safety hazard; if so, the equipment is taken out of service until corrected (1926.1412(d)(2)), and a safety device or operational aid defect needs the action in 1926.1415 and 1926.1416 before use (1926.1412(d)(3)). Deficiencies found at the annual/comprehensive inspection are handled by the qualified person under 1926.1412(f)(4) to (f)(6).
The manufacturer's inspection procedures (1926.1412(j)) and site rules may add checks or require them more often.

sections.title: Controls, lines, hooks and rope (each shift, monthly and annual)
items: No maladjustment interfering with proper operation
No apparent excessive wear of components; no contamination by lubricants, water or other foreign matter
Air, hydraulic and other pressurized lines
No deterioration or leakage, including on lines that flex in normal operation
Hydraulic system fluid at the proper level
No deformation, cracks, excessive wear, or damage from chemicals or heat
Reeving complies with the manufacturer's specifications
No malfunction, no apparent excessive deterioration, no dirt or moisture accumulation

sections.title: Setup, cab and safety devices (each shift, monthly and annual)
items: Properly inflated and in proper condition
Ground gives proper support; no settling under or around outriggers/stabilizers or foundations; no ground water accumulation (excludes general railroad system track regulated under 49 CFR part 213)
Equipment level within the manufacturer's tolerances before the shift and after each move and setup
No significant cracks, breaks or other deficiencies that would hamper the operator's view
Rails, rail stops, rail clamps and supporting surfaces (rail-travelling equipment)
Checked with no deficiency found (not required for Federal Railroad Administration-regulated track that is part of the general railroad system)

sections.title: Annual/comprehensive: structure, mechanical parts and power plant
items: Not deformed, cracked or significantly corroded
None loose, failed or significantly corroded
Pins, bearings, shafts, gears, rollers and locking devices
No distortion, cracks or significant wear
Brake and clutch parts, linings, pawls and ratchets
Safety device and operational aid accuracy
Operate properly with no significant inaccuracies
No safety-related problems such as leaking exhaust; emergency shut-down feature works; operates properly
No excessive sprocket wear or excessive chain stretch
Travel steering, brakes and locking devices

sections.title: Annual/comprehensive: tires, hydraulics, pads, electrics, labels and seat
items: Hydraulic, pneumatic and other pressurized hoses, fittings and tubing

No leak indications on flexible hose or at its junction with fittings; no leaks at threaded or clamped joints; hose outer covering free of blistering, abnormal deformation or other signs of failure; no excessive abrasion or scrubbing on hoses, rigid tubes or fittings
Hydraulic and pneumatic pumps and motors
No unusual noise or vibration, low operating speed, excessive fluid heating or low pressure; no loose bolts or fasteners; no leaks at shaft seals or joints between pump sections

Spools free of sticking and leaks and return properly to neutral; no leaks; no valve housing cracks; relief valves reach correct pressure, using the manufacturer's pressure-check procedure where one exists

No drifting from fluid leaking across the piston; no leaks at rod seals or welded joints; rods free of scores, nicks or dents; no significant dents in the case (barrel); rod eyes and connecting joints not loose or deformed
No cracked or split insulation; no loose or corroded terminations
All labels and decals originally supplied with the equipment by the manufacturer, or otherwise required under the standard, present and readable
Originally equipped operator seat (or equivalent) present

sections.title: Seat, access, functional test and records
items: Originally equipped steps, ladders, handrails and guards
Steps, ladders, handrails and guards condition
Equipment, as configured in the inspection, tested and functioning properly
Each deficiency the qualified person determined needs monitoring is checked in the monthly inspections
Record on file, kept at least 12 months by the employer that conducted the inspection
Record kept at least three months
Inspection documents within their retention period available to everyone who conducts inspections under 1926.1412

references: 29 CFR 1926.1412: Inspections (Part 1926 Subpart CC, Cranes and Derricks in Construction)
